The *Samathavāra* ("How each offense is settled") constitutes a chapter within the *Parivāra*, the concluding analytic treatise of the Pali *Vinaya Piṭaka*. The text systematically maps the Vinaya offenses and rules to the seven traditional legal procedures (*samatha* or *adhikaraṇasamatha*) employed for the settlement of monastic disputes and legal issues. Modern translations of the text include an English translation by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

None of the surveyed reference passages discuss this specific chapter of the *Parivāra*; they instead concern the meditative cultivation of serenity (*samatha*), the *Samathakkhandhaka* of the *Cullavagga*, the author Śamathadeva, or *adhikaraṇa-śamatha* in general non-canonical contexts.
